findings.where: Hero heading 'MARK · M · MOSELEY / INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR', the article title 'THE WORLD'S BEST PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP LAW', the 'CINZEL' specimen, the texture's painted 'M' and the motion sketch's 'LAID · WEIGHTY · SETTLED', all set in minium red, the same colour as the 'Write to Mark' button
findings.fault: The palette names minium as 'headings, the one action', so the one colour meant to point to the action is also on every large heading. Red no longer means 'act here'. In the hero the red heading, at about 60 px, outweighs the red button under it, so the squint order puts the heading first and the action second. This goes against the direction's own rule that the one accent flows to the action.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank staffer who has decided to get in touch and scans for how: the red that should lead the eye to 'Write to Mark' is spread over headings across the site. On an article page, the red title would be the strongest red in view while the contact action is weaker or missing.

findings.where: Hero, the 'Write to Mark' button (mailto:Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com), the page's one primary action
findings.fault: The only way to get in touch is a mailto link, and the address is not written anywhere on the page. If a visitor's computer has no mail program set up, the click seems to do nothing, and there is no address to copy instead.
findings.who_objects: An agency staffer on a locked-down work laptop or using webmail who clicks the page's one action, sees nothing happen, and has no visible address to fall back on. The page's single job is to get in touch with Mark, and this is where it fails.

findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote '“Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!”' set in a tabula ansata frame, the dovetail-handled shape that also frames the 'Write to Mark' button
findings.fault: One signature shape means two things: on the button it means 'this is the action', and on the pull quote it marks static text that does nothing. The direction card sets the tabula ansata as both button and pull quote, so this goes to the founder as a clash of one look across two functions. The quote's outlined version is the one an editor will repeat in every post, so the shape will stop marking the action.
findings.who_objects: A reader who has learned that the dovetail panel is the thing to click, and then meets the same panel around a quote in every article. Angélique would object too: each pull quote she adds puts another button-shaped panel on the page.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the 'LAY AGAIN' control (a button that replays the animation)
findings.fault: This button looks like a link: plain underlined text, the signifier this page gives the PDF link 'Streamlining the PPP Process…'. It does something in place instead of going anywhere, but it borrows the underline that links reserve. The tile therefore sets no distinct look for a quiet in-place action next to the filled primary button.
findings.who_objects: The layout and animation rounds, which take this tile's button and link looks as the system and would carry underlined button labels into the site. A visitor would object too, expecting an underlined phrase to take them somewhere.
